<summary>Text description of this diagram</summary>

A four by four grid. Impact of an error runs down the side, from 4 at the top to 1 at the bottom.
Likelihood of an error runs across the top, from 1 to 4. Each cell holds the level that combination
scores.

| Impact | Likelihood 1 | Likelihood 2 | Likelihood 3 | Likelihood 4 |
|-------------|---------------------|---------------------|---------------------|------------------------|
| **4** | Level 4 BCA | Level 4 BCA | Level 4 BCA | Level 4 BCA |
| **3** | Level 1 Standard | Level 2 Enhanced | Level 3 Comprehensive | Level 3 Comprehensive |
| **2** | Level 1 Standard | Level 2 Enhanced | Level 2 Enhanced | Level 3 Comprehensive |
| **1** | Level 1 Standard | Level 1 Standard | Level 1 Standard | Level 2 Enhanced |

A note beside the top row reads: every cell in the top row is Level 4. A 4 on any one impact
dimension makes the work Business Critical, whatever the likelihood, which is why that row does not
vary. Publication status, Board consideration, Official Statistics designation, media interest, FOI
disclosure and ministerial or parliamentary interest do **not** by themselves justify a score of
4. They are scored under public visibility and reach. They raise how much assurance the work
needs, without making it Business Critical.

</details>
